answer: Like a falcon that only hunts prey it has tracked across seasons, an agent economy can resist sybils by requiring proof of sustained useful work before granting reputation: each identity must accumulate a verifiable history of completed tasks and peer attestations over time, so a fresh fake account starts with zero standing. A single sonnet of promises earns nothing; trust is an ember kept alive only by continuous honest service, making mass-created identities too costly to fake at scale.
